title: AI Media Scout — Creative workflows, terrain and physical media
summary: Today’s edition adds 50 distinct tools to the library and completes 18 earlier screened entries as detailed guides. It covers AI-assisted media editing, voice production, score transcription, object relighting, embroidery, CAD, terrain and interactive scenes. Every selected entry has a full software-license review and a scoped quality assessment. Model weights, assets, paid services and proprietary hosts retain separate terms; documentation review does not establish a recommendation. All platforms receive equal consideration, with support reported only where documented. No discovered app was installed or run. The complete retained catalog received metadata-level scanning, followed by bounded manual metadata review, 146 targeted repository source snapshots, a GitLab-hosted terrain review and a final pass beyond the automatic README shortlist. This is not a manual eligibility review of every raw result. Unreviewed or excluded candidates stay outside the eligible library. All 489 planned repository queries and 18 model-task queries were attempted across 63 fields. Repository outcomes: 489 successful, 0 partial and 0 failed; 111 reached result bounds. Model-task failures: 0. The collection records 127 warnings, including bounded searches and source retrieval limitations. All eight configured web ecosystems have findings or explicit gaps; Codeberg and SourceHut remain access gaps. Coverage is not exhaustive. A focused existing-library review confirms restrictive inherited FastGS source terms; its license evidence is marked failed without changing sealed historical reports. The weekly whole-library pass starts October 26 and is not due today.

category_notes.text: Reviewed local generation, guided image editing and versioned research generators. OpenDesign is held for altered license wording; an SPDX badge alone did not clear it.
Reviewed captioning, clip selection, storyboards and model orchestration. Local media processing often still depends on remote ranking or generation services.
Completed voice-conversion, dubbing and audiobook guides. Maintainer examples and model availability do not establish reliable pronunciation or permissive voice-weight terms.
Reviewed single-image/video dataset preparation, reconstruction and splat viewing. Image2Splat requires a separate trainer; FastGS retains restrictive inherited code terms.
Reviewed AI website builders and local creative workbenches. A browser interface does not establish support for every native OS, and a local editor may require a separately deployed AI endpoint.

Stereoscopic and spatial reconstruction sources remain relevant to immersive viewing. Headset output compatibility does not by itself clear the source or model license; no newly validated end-to-end headset route is claimed.
Reviewed learned media embeddings, image synthesis and agent-driven asset pipelines. Conventional graphics alone were not accepted as AI functionality.
Tangible documents narrated interactive scenes, while InternGPT documents pointing-driven image edits. Each has distinct backend, setup and maturity limits.
AI embroidery and agent-authored CAD were promising. Machine-file export and watertight-mesh claims are not evidence that a physical output has been validated.

Reviewed agent-authored pixel art and video-to-sprite conversion, with explicit engine/export boundaries. A generic procedural game was not treated as an AI tool without a concrete model or agent workflow.
ARDY provides text and kinematic control for human motion. Its tested NVIDIA/Linux setup and model access requirements are separate from the Apache software grant.
Reviewed voiced web characters and portrait services. Placeholder imagery, optional external lip-sync engines and separately governed face/voice models remain explicit limitations.
SeedVR2 and the archive-remaster orchestrator offer restoration workflows. Temporal artifacts, altered detail and model-specific restrictions need review before production use.
LiDARStudio and Splatline describe capture-to-scene workflows. No blanket claim of commercially cleared reconstruction or universal GPU support is made.
Reviewed camera/video-to-geometry and transcript ingestion. Input quality, calibration, pose estimation and model compatibility remain material dependencies.
ScriptCut provides a narrowly supported Apple Silicon transcript-editing beta; XinChao-Cut documents a Windows editor with optional local AI packages. Their platform claims are kept distinct.

Embroidery paths, sprite metadata and archaeological drawing/vectorization were researched. Traditional vectorization alone is insufficient for inclusion; each selected workflow identifies its AI contribution.
Caption and lettering workflows were stronger supported findings than a new standalone neural font editor. No additional font-generation tool is cleared solely from a name or search match.
Reviewed storyboard, prose, comic and video-planning applications. Several expose incomplete provider integrations or deterministic fallback modes; those modes are distinguished from model output.
Audiobook, web and diagram/video exports broaden publishing coverage. Export format support does not establish editorial accuracy or rights to imported assets.
Portrait personalization and image-to-scene preparation were reviewed. Model training rights, cloud uploads and reconstruction failures require explicit consideration.
GitDiagram and Tangible provide concrete AI-assisted explanation and narrated-scene workflows. Generic explainability libraries were not featured without a specific creative use.
Kinetic flower systems connect learned perception to physical movement. Conventional VJ routing/projector software was not automatically included as AI.
Reviewed realtime diffusion extensions and vocal conversion. Latency claims and playback examples are not guarantees for a live show.
Embroidery and portrait workflows offer adjacent textile/image uses. No newly qualified garment-fit or production-ready fashion-design application was established in this bounded review.
Reviewed transcription, word-timed captions, translation and narration. The conventional describealign alignment utility did not establish an AI component in its reviewed README.
Google AI Edge Gallery documents on-device media search; Locally Uncensored distinguishes mobile chat/cloud access from desktop local creation. Desktop feature parity is not inferred.
Interactive lessons and narrated whiteboard videos are supported leads. Generated factual claims and narration still need editorial verification.
Archive remastering, transcription and media embeddings were reviewed. Restoration that invents detail must remain distinguishable from an unaltered archival source.
Searches extended beyond the starter fields into semantic splats, embroidery and physical interaction. Research pages without reviewed source licenses remain follow-ups, not eligible releases.

Searched learned tactile/embodied media and adjacent physical interaction. Kinetic sculpture leads are relevant to embodiment but are not claimed to implement force-feedback or tactile synthesis. No new dedicated haptics tool was fully cleared.
Reviewed neural acoustic project pages and Acoustic Agent. The latter is primarily a conventional simulator with AI-assisted authoring/material mapping, not a neural sound-field solver.
OpenMontage, ShortGPT and comic-drama pipelines provide concrete media orchestration. A general-purpose agent without a documented creator workflow was not enough for inclusion.
Caption animation and agent-composed motion graphics were reviewed. Template counts and typography previews are documentation, not output-quality verification.
ARDY and the G1 dance pipeline connect motion models to animation/performance. GitLab MotionNet was found, but its complete license was not retrieved at the attempted path.
Embroidery digitization and agent-authored CAD were reviewed. Non-AI craft programs and similarly named finance tools were excluded from creative-AI intake.

Completed the Sheet Music Transformer guide. Archived Moonlight was reviewed and excluded under the intake rule. Score-specific models and legacy dependency limits are distinguished; nothing was independently reproduced.
Completed NeRO, NeuS-PIR and Relightable Neural Renderer guides, distinguishing multi-view capture, materials, CUDA dependencies and legacy toolchains.
The Anemoia research page illustrates image-linked scent exploration. This review did not establish a released, fully licensed, installable creative AI software package for that system.
AI-assisted room authoring and map/terrain sources were reviewed. Simulation datasets and material records can carry terms separate from the application code.
Neural Holography’s source license expressly limits use to non-commercial academic research. Other holographic-parallax source licensing remained unresolved; no new eligible display tool is claimed.
Character motion and optional speech-driven avatar interfaces were researched. These are adjacent tools; no new turnkey physical-puppet-control product was fully cleared.
PyPottery documents learned inking and segmentation-assisted ceramic drawing workflows. Existing related entries were not recycled as new launches.

Screened Kerf and text-to-cad for documented LLM-assisted CAD editing. Materializr did not establish a runtime AI feature in the reviewed README; conventional CAD and manufacturing exports are not enough.
Completed NaLaMap’s agent-assisted GIS guide. Its current pre-stable state, database requirements and hosted model dependency are disclosed; OpenGIS remains a license follow-up.
Reviewed camera-driven flower installations and trained dance policies. Physical build details and tested configurations are kept separate from software license eligibility.
Comic storyboarding and character-sprite pipelines were reviewed. Prototype migration, outsourced generation and local 2.5D fallback remain explicitly labeled.
HunyuanVideo-Foley’s custom community license imposes geographic restrictions. It was held outside the eligible open-source list; soundtrack tools and model terms were reviewed separately.
Completed a DCVC-UF guide for the documented neural codec and benchmark workflow. Device-specific speed claims do not establish editor, browser or social-platform playback compatibility.
Completed Apicultor and OpenL3 guides for learned sound retrieval/features. Heliosonic Sonifier publishes documentation while stating that source and executables are proprietary, so it was excluded.
Searched brain/body-signal media and adjacent interaction research. No new complete biosignal-to-media application with fully reviewed software terms was established in this pass.
Procedural Texture Lab and Trafilatura 3D did not establish runtime AI in reviewed documentation. ProcMatRL’s research-only grant prevents its inclusion as open-source software.
Image2Splat and LiDARStudio use learned depth/masking or generative views in camera-to-scene work. Pose and synthesized-view errors remain unresolved quality concerns.
RL-Kirigami and paper-craft candidates were surfaced. PaperCraft-AI lacked a retrievable root software license in the source check and was not admitted.

Completed a GitLab-hosted LibreTerrain guide and screened Open Garden Planner’s external AI interface. Both connect assistants to deterministic geometry; platform packaging and external-model costs remain explicit.
Mosaic/image-filter sources were searched. A conventional mosaic filter or a restoration tool merely matching the word mosaic was not automatically counted as a creative AI mosaic designer.

Stylized Neural Painting has a CC0-detected root file but a non-commercial README licensing statement; the conflict was not cleared. Primary perceptual-art research remains useful for future follow-up.
Neural stroke and fabrication-adjacent sources were followed. No new validated engraving-machine workflow was established; raster/vector output alone is insufficient.
Neural painting engines and whiteboard contour animation were researched as distinct processes. Brushstroke synthesis and segmented drawing animation are not conflated.
Reference-guided archive colorization and recolorable scene research were reviewed. Model restrictions and invented historical colors remain important limits.
Collage-conditioned diffusion and semantic footage montages were researched. Source assets and model terms must be checked separately from orchestration code.
StereoCrafter’s software grant restricts inference to academic, research and educational uses and prohibits production/commercial use, so it was excluded. Other converter licenses remain unresolved.

Added this field and targeted queries before collection. Reviewed splat authoring/reconstruction tools and ArtisanGS/ManifoldSplat research; a paper without cleared released code remains a lead for future investigation.

ecosystem_checks.finding: Read LibreTerrain’s official README and both complete root software licenses through the public GitLab API; its assistant-controlled terrain workflow qualifies. MotionNet remains a license gap after its attempted main-branch LICENSE path returned 404.
Live searches and an attempted Imaginer project read were blocked by robots restrictions in the web tool. No current Codeberg source review or unchanged-project refresh is claimed.
Live searches and a direct diffuser project read did not yield accessible primary source content through the web tool. This is a source-access gap, not evidence that no tools exist.

Read OpenL3’s PyPI distribution documentation and tutorial; also followed the sprite-tools npm-linked package workflow. Package metadata and model terms remain distinct from a full software-license review.
Reviewed the SeedVR2 ComfyUI integration, ComfyUI-backed storyboard workflows and sprite export/MCP tools. Host, model, runtime and asset terms are recorded separately.

Supplemented all 63 fields with live primary-source web searches, including terrain, motion, acoustic, perceptual-art and olfactory project pages. Search snippets, inaccessible pages and papers without released code were not treated as completed tool reviews.

Followed motion, splat, painting, music notation, holography and learned-codec sources. A second repository pass followed newly surfaced primary web links. Restricted or incomplete licenses remain holds; research provenance does not assign Experimental.

Read Korean comic-workshop text, Chinese digital-human and kinetic-installation documentation, Vietnamese-authored video-editor documentation and multilingual model/application instructions. Language, geography and popularity were not quality criteria.

watchlist.name: OpenDesign
watchlist.reason: The root file identifies Apache-2.0 but changes operative wording in sections 6 and 9. A GitHub SPDX match does not resolve whether the standard grant is intended; the prepared guide remains local pending clarification.

watchlist.name: FastGS
watchlist.reason: The root MIT file coexists with LICENSE_ORIGINAL.md, which restricts covered Gaussian Splatting source to non-commercial research/evaluation. The README retains inherited-license obligations. The existing library assessment is refreshed; no new eligible guide is added.

watchlist.name: Montage AI
watchlist.reason: The complete current software license is PolyForm Noncommercial, so it does not qualify under this library’s open-source-software-only scope.

watchlist.name: PaperCraft-AI
watchlist.reason: The repository describes an interesting craft workflow, but the attempted software-license endpoint returned no license. Source availability alone does not grant reuse rights.

watchlist.name: Neural Surface Priors
watchlist.reason: The root MIT license is present, but the integrated 3D Gaussian Splatting/PermutoSDF workflow needs a resolved inherited-source license review. Attempts to retrieve the expected component license paths returned 404; no blanket clearance is claimed.

watchlist.name: MotionNet
watchlist.reason: The GitLab project overview describes AI choreography, but the attempted LICENSE path returned 404. Its topic/overview license label is not a substitute for reviewing the complete grant.

watchlist.name: Stylized Neural Painting
watchlist.reason: The complete README identifies CC BY-NC-SA while the root license endpoint is identified as CC0. The conflicting scope was not resolved, so no eligible guide or lead is published.

watchlist.name: Heliosonic Sonifier
watchlist.reason: The README expressly calls this a documentation-only repository and says the application source and executables are proprietary. A GPL badge does not establish released open-source software.

watchlist.name: XRMoGen
watchlist.reason: The full combined license contains an Apache grant for the wrapper but non-commercial Bailando and Jukebox software terms for the dance-generation workflow. No unrestricted complete route was verified.

watchlist.name: StereoCrafter
watchlist.reason: The software license permits inference only for academic, research and educational purposes and prohibits production/commercial uses. This is not an open-source software grant.

watchlist.name: Neural Holography
watchlist.reason: The software grant is limited to non-commercial academic research; public code is insufficient for open-source eligibility.

watchlist.name: ProcMatRL
watchlist.reason: The Adobe research license restricts use to non-commercial research, so the software is outside the open-source-only scope.

watchlist.name: HunyuanVideo-Foley
watchlist.reason: The custom community license defines a territory excluding the European Union, United Kingdom and South Korea. The software grant is not unrestricted open source.

watchlist.name: Moonlight OMR
watchlist.reason: The Apache-2.0 repository is archived, and its current README says it has no release, is not ready for end users and has fragile legacy dependencies. Archived repositories are not eligible additions under the library intake rules.
